title: The 把 disposal sentence
pattern: 主语 + 把 + 宾语 + 动词 + 其他成分
explanation: 把 (bǎ) moves the object in front of the verb when you want to emphasize what happens to it. The verb can't stand alone after 把 — it usually needs a complement, 了, or a repeated verb to show the result. This structure is common whenever an action changes, moves, or finishes something specific.

title: The 被 passive sentence
pattern: 受事 + 被 + (施事) + 动词 + 其他成分
explanation: 被 (bèi) marks the passive voice: the subject is the receiver of the action, not the doer. The person or thing doing the action can go right after 被, or be left out if it isn't important. Like 把, the verb after 被 usually needs a complement or 了 to sound complete.

title: Purpose with 为了
pattern: 为了 + 目的，(主语) + 动词短语
explanation: 为了 (wèile) introduces the goal or purpose of an action, like English "in order to". It sits at the very start of the sentence, before the goal, and the main clause with the actual action follows. Unlike 因为...所以, 为了 gives a reason you are aiming for, not a cause that already happened.

title: Just, merely with 只是
pattern: (主语) + 只是 + 动词/形容词短语
explanation: 只是 (zhǐshì) means "just, merely, only" — it softens a statement by saying something is nothing more than what's mentioned. It often appears in explanations that downplay a situation, narrowing the claim to one small fact.

title: Even... with 连...都/也
pattern: 连 + 名词/短语 + 都/也 + 动词短语
explanation: 连 (lián) highlights an extreme example, usually paired with 都 or 也 before the verb, to mean "even". It's often used with a negative verb to stress how surprising or extreme something is — for example, "even I don't know".

title: Only if... then with 只有...才
pattern: 只有 + 条件，(主语) + 才 + 结果
explanation: 只有 (zhǐyǒu) states the one necessary condition for something to happen, and 才 (cái) in the result clause means "only then". Together they say a result can happen in no other way except through this one condition — a stronger, more exclusive version of 如果...就.

title: Formal causative with 使
pattern: A + 使 + B + 形容词/动词短语
explanation: 使 (shǐ) is a more formal, written way to say 让 or 叫 — "to make/cause someone or something to be a certain way". It's common in written Chinese, news, and essays, often followed by an adjective or a change-of-state verb rather than a concrete action.

title: Of course with 当然
pattern: (主语) + 当然 + 动词/形容词短语
explanation: 当然 (dāngrán) means "of course, naturally" — used to confirm something is obviously true or to agree enthusiastically. It usually goes right before the verb or adjective, and can also stand alone as a reply meaning "Of course!".

title: Extremely with 形容词 + 极了
pattern: 形容词 + 极了
explanation: 极了 (jíle) goes right after an adjective to mean "extremely, to the max" — a stronger, more colloquial version of 很 or 非常. It always comes after the adjective, never before, and often ends the sentence.

title: Finally with 终于
pattern: (主语) + 终于 + 动词短语 + 了
explanation: 终于 (zhōngyú) means "finally, at last" — it marks the end of a long wait or effort, usually paired with 了 at the end of the sentence. It carries a sense of relief or achievement after something difficult or long-awaited.

title: In addition to with 除了...还/也
pattern: 除了 + A，(主语) + 还/也 + B
explanation: 除了 (chúle) here means "in addition to, besides" rather than "except" — paired with 还 or 也 in the second clause, it adds more information on top of what's mentioned. This differs from 除了...以外，都, which means "except for".

title: Suddenly with 突然
pattern: (主语) + 突然 + 动词短语
explanation: 突然 (tūrán) describes something happening suddenly, without warning. It can go before the subject or right before the verb, and often appears with 了 to mark a sudden change.

title: Therefore with 因此
pattern: ..., 因此 + 结果
explanation: 因此 (yīncǐ) means "therefore, as a result" — a more formal, written alternative to 所以. It links a reason already stated to a resulting conclusion, and is common in essays, news, and explanations.

title: Once, in the past with 曾经
pattern: (主语) + 曾经 + 动词短语
explanation: 曾经 (céngjīng) marks that something happened at some point in the past, but may not still be true — like English "once, at one time". It goes before the verb and pairs naturally with 过 to show past experience.

title: Pressing for an answer with 到底
pattern: 到底 + 疑问句
explanation: 到底 (dàodǐ) adds emphasis to a question, meaning "exactly, on earth, after all" — it shows the speaker really wants to know the answer. It usually sits right before the question word or verb.

title: Continuing on with V + 下去
pattern: 动词 + 下去
explanation: 下去 (xiàqù) after a verb shows that an ongoing action will continue into the future — "keep on doing something". It's often used to encourage someone to persist, or to describe something that keeps happening.

title: Moreover with 并且
pattern: ..., 并且 + 补充信息
explanation: 并且 (bìngqiě) links two related actions or facts happening together, meaning "and, moreover, furthermore". It's more formal than 而且 and often joins two verb phrases describing the same subject.

title: Sequencing with 首先...然后
pattern: 首先 + 第一步，然后 + 第二步
explanation: 首先 (shǒuxiān) means "first of all" and introduces the first step of a process; 然后 (ránhòu) then introduces what comes next. Together they help you lay out instructions or a story in clear order.

title: At least with 至少
pattern: 至少 + 数量/程度
explanation: 至少 (zhìshǎo) means "at least" — it sets a minimum amount, time, or degree, showing that the real number could be higher. It usually comes right before the quantity or requirement it's describing.

title: Causing a result with 造成
pattern: 原因 + 造成 + (不好的)结果
explanation: 造成 (zàochéng) means "to cause, bring about" — usually followed by a negative or serious result, like a problem, loss, or injury. It's a formal verb often used in news reports and explanations.

title: Formal cause with 由于
pattern: 由于 + 原因，(主语) + 结果
explanation: 由于 (yóuyú) is a formal way to say "because of, due to" — common in written Chinese and news. Like 因为, it can start the sentence, but it can also come directly before a short noun phrase rather than a full clause.

title: Facing a challenge with 面对
pattern: 面对 + 困难/问题，(主语) + 动词短语
explanation: 面对 (miànduì) means "to face, confront" — usually followed by something difficult like a problem or challenge. It's often used at the start of a sentence to show how someone responds to a situation.

title: Still, as before with 仍然
pattern: (主语) + 仍然 + 动词/形容词短语
explanation: 仍然 (réngrán) means "still, as before" — it shows that a situation hasn't changed even though something might have been expected to change it. It's more formal than 还.

title: Worth doing with 值得
pattern: (这/那) + 值得 + 动词
explanation: 值得 (zhídé) means "to be worth (doing)" — followed directly by a verb, it says an action is worthwhile. It's often used to recommend something, like a book, a movie, or a way of doing things.

title: Only, merely with 仅/仅仅
pattern: 仅(仅) + 数量/范围
explanation: 仅 (jǐn) or its doubled form 仅仅 (jǐnjǐn) means "only, merely" — a formal way to limit a number or scope, similar to 只 but more written in style. It usually comes right before the number or fact being limited.

title: Originally with 本来
pattern: (主语) + 本来 + 想/是/要 + ..., 后来/但是 + 转变
explanation: 本来 (běnlái) means "originally, at first" — it sets up what someone planned or believed before things changed. It's often followed by a contrast showing what actually happened instead.

title: Rhetorical questions with 难道...吗
pattern: 难道 + 主语 + 动词短语 + 吗？
explanation: 难道 (nándào) turns a statement into a rhetorical question that expects the opposite answer — like saying "Don't tell me...?" or "Surely not...?" in English. It often pairs with 吗 at the end, and shows the speaker's surprise or disbelief.

title: Fairly, quite with 相当
pattern: 相当 + 形容词
explanation: 相当 (xiāngdāng) means "fairly, quite, considerably" — a bit stronger and more formal than 很, describing a fairly high degree. It goes right before an adjective.

title: Even more with 更加
pattern: 更加 + 形容词/动词
explanation: 更加 (gèngjiā) means "even more" — a more formal, written version of 更, used to show an increase compared to before. It goes right before the adjective or verb being intensified.

title: Never with 从来不/没
pattern: (主语) + 从来 + 不/没 + 动词
explanation: 从来 (cónglái) means "ever, always" and is nearly always paired with 不 or 没 to mean "never". It emphasizes that something has (or hasn't) been true the entire time, without exception.

title: Any... at all with 任何...都
pattern: 任何 + 名词 + 都 + 动词短语
explanation: 任何 (rènhé) means "any" in the broadest sense — "any at all, no matter which one". It's almost always followed by 都 before the verb to stress that the statement applies without exception.

title: Not until... with 直到...才
pattern: 直到 + 时间/事件，(主语) + 才 + 结果
explanation: 直到 (zhídào) means "until, up to" — paired with 才 in the main clause, it says something didn't happen until a certain point. It stresses how long you had to wait for the result.

title: A casual if with 要是...就
pattern: 要是 + 条件，(主语) + 就 + 结果
explanation: 要是 (yàoshi) is a colloquial way of saying "if", used mostly in spoken Chinese instead of 如果. The result clause still uses 就 to mean "then", just like with 如果...就.

title: According to with 按照
pattern: 按照 + 标准/规定，(主语) + 动词短语
explanation: 按照 (ànzhào) means "according to, in accordance with" — it introduces a rule, standard, or plan that an action follows. It usually starts the sentence, before the subject.

title: Obviously with 显然
pattern: 显然，... / (主语) + 显然 + 动词/形容词短语
explanation: 显然 (xiǎnrán) means "obviously, clearly" — used when a conclusion is easy to see from the facts. It can start the sentence or sit right before the verb or adjective.

title: Having no choice with 不得不
pattern: (主语) + 不得不 + 动词短语
explanation: 不得不 (bùdébù) means "can't help but, have no choice but to" — it shows the subject is forced into an action by circumstances, not by their own will. It goes right before the verb.

title: Probably, roughly with 大概
pattern: 大概 + 数量/情况
explanation: 大概 (dàgài) means "probably, roughly, approximately" — used when giving an estimate rather than an exact number or fact. It usually comes before a number, time, or guess about a situation.

title: Gradually, slowly with 慢慢
pattern: (主语) + 慢慢 + (地) + 动词
explanation: 慢慢 (mànmàn) means "slowly, gradually" — it can describe the physical speed of an action or a gradual change over time. It often takes 地 before the verb in careful writing, though 地 is often dropped in speech.

title: In fact with 事实上
pattern: 事实上，...
explanation: 事实上 (shìshí shang) means "in fact, actually" — it introduces the real situation, often correcting a wrong impression given earlier. It typically starts the sentence.

title: Breaking something with V + 坏
pattern: 动词 + 坏 (+ 了)
explanation: 坏 (huài) after a verb shows that the action ruined or broke something — "break, ruin, spoil" as a result. It's a classic resultative complement, always attached right after the verb.

title: Potential complement: V + 得/不 + 了
pattern: 动词 + 得/不 + 了
explanation: 得 or 不 between a verb and 了 asks or states whether an action is possible to complete — "can/can't manage to do something". 得了 (de liǎo) means it's possible, and 不了 (bu liǎo) means it isn't, often because of a physical or practical limit.

title: Assigning responsibility with 由
pattern: 事情 + 由 + 人 + 负责/决定/做
explanation: 由 (yóu) marks who is responsible for something or who will carry it out — "by, from" in the sense of assigning a task. It goes right before the person in charge.

title: Not only... but also with 不仅...还/也
pattern: 不仅 + A，(主语) + 还/也 + B
explanation: 不仅 (bùjǐn) means "not only" — like 不但, it's followed by 还 or 也 to add a second, often stronger point. 不仅 is a little more formal and common in writing.

title: Simply, virtually with 简直
pattern: (主语) + 简直 + 形容词/动词短语
explanation: 简直 (jiǎnzhí) means "simply, virtually, practically" — used for exaggeration, showing something is almost too much to believe. It goes right before the adjective or verb it emphasizes, often with 了 at the end.

title: Anyway, in any case with 反正
pattern: 反正 + 主语 + 动词短语
explanation: 反正 (fǎnzhèng) means "anyway, in any case" — it shows that no matter what happens, the outcome or attitude stays the same. It's common in casual speech to dismiss other possibilities.

title: I'm afraid that... with 恐怕
pattern: 恐怕 + 不好的猜测
explanation: 恐怕 (kǒngpà) means "I'm afraid that..., probably" — used to soften a negative guess or worry, showing the speaker isn't fully certain but expects something unwelcome.

title: As much as possible with 尽量
pattern: 尽量 + 动词短语
explanation: 尽量 (jǐnliàng) means "as much/far as possible" — it encourages doing something to the greatest extent one can. It goes right before the verb, often in requests or advice.

title: Promptly, in time with 及时
pattern: 及时 + 动词
explanation: 及时 (jíshí) means "promptly, in time" — it describes doing something at just the right moment, without delay. It usually comes right before the verb.

title: In a row with 连续
pattern: 连续 + 数量 + 量词 + 名词
explanation: 连续 (liánxù) means "continuous, in a row" — placed before a number and measure word, it shows something repeats without a break. It's common for describing streaks, like consecutive days or wins.

title: Usually, normally with 通常
pattern: (主语) + 通常 + 动词短语
explanation: 通常 (tōngcháng) means "usually, normally" — it describes what typically happens, similar to 一般. It goes before the verb, often at the start of a sentence about daily habits.

title: Each other, mutually with 互相
pattern: (双方) + 互相 + 动词
explanation: 互相 (hùxiāng) means "each other, mutually" — it goes before a verb to show that two or more people do the same action to one another. It's often used with verbs like 帮助, 认识, 关心.

title: In person with 亲自
pattern: (主语) + 亲自 + 动词
explanation: 亲自 (qīnzì) means "personally, in person" — it emphasizes that someone did something themselves, rather than through someone else. It goes right before the verb.

title: To seem, appear with 显得
pattern: (主语) + 显得 + 形容词
explanation: 显得 (xiǎnde) means "to appear, seem, look" — it's followed by an adjective describing how someone or something comes across, based on how they act or look.

title: Taking the initiative with 主动
pattern: (主语) + 主动 + 动词
explanation: 主动 (zhǔdòng) means "to take the initiative, proactively" — it describes doing something without being asked or forced. It goes right before the verb.

title: Turning into with 把...V成
pattern: 主语 + 把 + 宾语 + 动词 + 成 + 结果
explanation: Adding 成 (chéng) after the verb in a 把 sentence shows the object was changed into something new — "turn A into B". It's a common extension of the basic 把 structure for talking about transformations, exchanges, or writing something as something else.

title: Giving to someone with 把...V给
pattern: 主语 + 把 + 宾语 + 动词 + 给 + 对象
explanation: Adding 给 (gěi) after the verb in a 把 sentence shows the object ends up with someone — "do X to it and give it to someone". It's common with verbs like 送, 还, 卖, 发 that involve handing something over.

title: Informal passive with 叫/让
pattern: 受事 + 叫/让 + 施事 + 动词 + 其他成分
explanation: In casual speech, 叫 (jiào) and 让 (ràng) can work just like 被 to mark a passive sentence — the subject has something done to it by someone else. This is common in everyday conversation, while 被 sounds more formal or written.

title: Potential complement: V + 得/不 + 下
pattern: 动词 + 得/不 + 下
explanation: 得 or 不 plus 下 after a verb asks whether something has enough room or capacity — "fit, hold". 得下 (de xià) means there's enough space, and 不下 (bu xià) means there isn't.

title: Formal comparison with 较
pattern: 较 + 形容词
explanation: 较 (jiào) is a formal, written way to say "relatively, comparatively" — similar to 比较 but shorter and more common in reports or writing. It goes right before an adjective.

title: All along with 始终
pattern: (主语) + 始终 + 动词/形容词短语
explanation: 始终 (shǐzhōng) means "all along, from beginning to end" — it emphasizes that something stayed the same the whole time, without changing. It's more formal than 一直.

title: Just as expected with 果然
pattern: (主语) + 果然 + 动词/形容词短语
explanation: 果然 (guǒrán) means "sure enough, just as expected" — used when something turns out exactly as predicted or guessed. It goes right before the verb or adjective.

title: Left with no choice but with 只好
pattern: (主语) + 只好 + 动词短语
explanation: 只好 (zhǐhǎo) means "to have no choice but to, to have to settle for" — used when the best option left isn't ideal. Compared to 不得不, 只好 focuses more on settling for the only option that remains.

title: No matter what with 不论...都
pattern: 不论 + 疑问词/选择，(主语) + 都 + 结果
explanation: 不论 (bùlùn) means "no matter, regardless of" — often followed by a question word like 谁/什么/怎么 or an either-or choice, with 都 in the result clause. It shows the outcome stays the same in every case.

title: Often, tends to with 往往
pattern: (主语) + 往往 + 动词短语
explanation: 往往 (wǎngwǎng) means "often, tends to" — it describes a pattern based on past experience or general observation, not a fixed habit like 常常. It goes before the verb.

title: It's said that with 据说
explanation: 据说 (jùshuō) means "it's said that, reportedly" — used to share information you heard from others, without confirming it yourself. It starts the sentence.

title: Looks like with 看起来/看上去
pattern: (主语) + 看起来/看上去 + 形容词
explanation: 看起来 (kàn qǐlái) and 看上去 (kàn shàngqù) both mean "it looks like, it seems" — describing an impression based on appearance. They go right before an adjective, and are used interchangeably.

title: Up to now with 至今
pattern: (主语) + 至今 + 还/仍然 + 没有/动词短语
explanation: 至今 (zhìjīn) means "up to now, so far" — it marks a situation that has continued from the past into the present. It's often paired with 还 or 没有.

title: Back then with 当初
pattern: 当初，(主语) + 动词短语
explanation: 当初 (dāngchū) means "originally, back then" — it looks back at a past decision or situation, often used when reflecting on whether that past choice was right. It starts the sentence or clause.

title: Holding firm with V + 住
pattern: 动词 + 住
explanation: 住 (zhù) after a verb shows an action makes something stay in place or fixed — "catch and hold, remember firmly, stop". It's a common resultative complement, seen in words like 抓住 (catch hold of) and 记住 (remember firmly).

title: Starting to with 形容词/动词 + 起来
pattern: 形容词/动词 + 起来
explanation: 起来 (qǐlái) after an adjective or verb can mark the start of a new state — "start to become, get into doing". Unlike its literal sense of standing up, here it shows a change beginning and continuing.

title: The more... the more... with 越...越...
pattern: 越 + A，越 + B
explanation: 越...越... (yuè...yuè...) links two changes that happen together — "the more A, the more B". Both clauses use 越 before a verb or adjective, showing they rise or fall in step.

title: Negative comparison with 没有
pattern: A + 没有 + B + (这么/那么) + 形容词
explanation: 没有 (méiyǒu) can make a comparison negative — "A is not as [adjective] as B". It's a common alternative to 不比, often paired with 这么 or 那么 before the adjective.

title: Doing two things at once with 一边...一边...
pattern: 一边 + 动词1，一边 + 动词2
explanation: 一边...一边... (yìbiān...yìbiān...) shows two actions happening at the same time, done by the same person — "while doing A, also doing B". Both verbs go right after 一边.

title: Both... and... with 又...又...
pattern: 又 + 形容词1，又 + 形容词2
explanation: 又...又... (yòu...yòu...) links two qualities or actions that are both true at the same time — "both A and B". It's often used with two adjectives describing the same subject.

title: As soon as... then... with 一...就...
pattern: 一 + 动词1，就 + 动词2
explanation: 一...就... (yī...jiù...) links two actions that happen right after each other — "as soon as A happens, B happens". The first verb follows 一, and the second follows 就.

title: Relative clauses with 的
pattern: 动词短语 + 的 + 名词
explanation: 的 (de) can turn a whole verb phrase into a description of a noun, like an English relative clause — "the book [that] I bought", "the person [who] is singing". The descriptive clause comes first, then 的, then the noun it modifies.

title: The 所 nominalizer in formal writing
pattern: (主语) + 所 + 动词 + 的 + 名词
explanation: 所 (suǒ) can go right before a verb in formal or written Chinese, turning the verb phrase into something like "what/that which [subject] verbs". It's most often followed by 的 and a noun, and mainly used with two-syllable verbs like 说, 做, 想, 知道.

title: A whole, full amount with 整整
pattern: 整整 + 数量 + 量词
explanation: 整整 (zhěngzhěng) emphasizes that an amount is a full, whole quantity — "a whole..., a full...". It goes right before the number and measure word, stressing there's no less than that.

title: Over and over with 反复
pattern: 反复 + 动词
explanation: 反复 (fǎnfù) means "repeatedly, over and over again" — it describes an action done many times to make sure it's right. It goes right before the verb.

title: Already, long since with 早已
pattern: (主语) + 早已 + 动词短语 + 了
explanation: 早已 (zǎoyǐ) means "already, long since" — a stronger, more formal version of 已经, showing that something happened a long time before now. It goes right before the verb.

title: On one hand... on the other hand... with 一方面...另一方面...
pattern: 一方面 + A，另一方面 + B
explanation: 一方面...另一方面... (yī fāngmiàn...lìng yī fāngmiàn...) presents two sides of a situation — "on one hand..., on the other hand...". It's common in formal explanations that weigh different factors.

title: Resolutely with 坚决
pattern: (主语) + 坚决 + 动词短语
explanation: 坚决 (jiānjué) means "resolutely, firmly" — describing an action or decision made with strong, unwavering determination. It goes right before the verb.

title: Inevitably with 必然
pattern: (主语) + 必然 + 动词短语
explanation: 必然 (bìrán) means "inevitably, necessarily" — it shows a result that's bound to happen given the situation, with no real alternative. It's formal and common in writing.

title: Commonly, widely with 普遍
pattern: 普遍 + 动词/形容词
explanation: 普遍 (pǔbiàn) means "widely, commonly, universally" — describing something true for most people or cases, not just a few. It goes right before the verb or adjective.

title: Totaling, altogether with 共有
pattern: (地方/范围) + 共有 + 数量 + 名词
explanation: 共有 (gòngyǒu) means "to have a total of, altogether there are" — used when counting up everything in a group. It goes right before the total number and noun.

title: What for? with 干吗
pattern: 干吗 + 动词短语？
explanation: 干吗 (gànmá) is a casual way to ask "what for, why" — often showing a bit of surprise or mild complaint about someone's action. It's common in spoken Chinese.

title: Around a time with 前后
pattern: 时间/节日 + 前后
explanation: 前后 (qiánhòu) after a time word or festival name means "around, or so" — showing the event happens close to that point, a bit before or after. It comes right after the time expression.

title: Not only... but also with 不光...还/也
pattern: 不光 + A，(主语) + 还/也 + B
explanation: 不光 (bùguāng) is a casual, spoken way to say "not only" — just like 不但 and 不仅, it pairs with 还 or 也 in the next clause to add more information.

title: Nearly, close to with 将近
pattern: 将近 + 数量
explanation: 将近 (jiāngjìn) means "nearly, close to" — it goes right before a number, showing the real amount is just short of it. It's often used for quantities, distances, or lengths of time.

title: Hastily, at once with 连忙
pattern: (主语) + 连忙 + 动词短语
explanation: 连忙 (liánmáng) means "hastily, at once" — describing a quick reaction to something that just happened. It goes right before the verb, often at the start of a response in a story.

title: Plenty of with 有的是
pattern: (某地方) + 有的是 + 名词
explanation: 有的是 (yǒudeshì) means "there's plenty of, no shortage of" — used to reassure someone there's more than enough of something. It replaces 有 when you want to stress abundance.

title: Placing something with 把...V在
pattern: 主语 + 把 + 宾语 + 动词 + 在 + 地点
explanation: Adding 在 (zài) after the verb in a 把 sentence shows exactly where the object ends up — "do X to it, ending up at this place". It's common with verbs like 放, 写, 挂, 停.

title: Whatever you do... with 千万
pattern: 千万 + 不要/别 + 动词短语
explanation: 千万 (qiānwàn) adds strong emphasis to a warning or request — "whatever you do, be sure to (not)...". It's almost always paired with 不要 or 别 right before the verb.

title: Possessing formally with 具有
pattern: (主语) + 具有 + 抽象名词
explanation: 具有 (jùyǒu) is a formal way to say "to possess, to have" — used with abstract qualities or characteristics rather than physical objects. It's common in written or professional Chinese.

title: Approximately with 大约
pattern: 大约 + 数量
explanation: 大约 (dàyuē) means "approximately, about" — used before a number or time to show it's an estimate, not exact. It's similar to 大概 but a little more common right before precise numbers.

title: Heading to with 前往
pattern: (主语) + 前往 + 地点
explanation: 前往 (qiánwǎng) is a formal, written way to say "to head to, to go to" — used instead of 去 in news, announcements, and formal writing.

title: Hurry up and... with 赶快
pattern: 赶快 + 动词短语
explanation: 赶快 (gǎnkuài) means "hurry up and, quickly" — used to urge someone to act fast, often in a request or command. It goes right before the verb.

title: Basically, by and large with 基本上
pattern: (主语) + 基本上 + 动词/形容词短语
explanation: 基本上 (jīběn shang) means "basically, by and large" — it shows something is mostly true or mostly finished, allowing for small exceptions. It goes before the verb or adjective.

title: Expected to with 预计
pattern: 预计 + 主语 + 动词短语
explanation: 预计 (yùjì) means "to estimate, to expect" — used before a prediction about the future, like a schedule, weather, or result. It usually starts the sentence.

title: Listing steps with 首先...其次...最后
pattern: 首先 + 第一点，其次 + 第二点，最后 + 第三点
explanation: This three-part sequence lays out steps clearly: 首先 (shǒuxiān) for the first point, 其次 (qícì) for the next, and 最后 (zuìhòu) for the last. It's very common in speeches, instructions, and essays.

title: On one's own accord with 自觉
pattern: (主语) + 自觉 (地) + 动词短语
explanation: 自觉 (zìjué) means "consciously, on one's own initiative" — describing someone who does the right thing without being told or watched. It goes right before the verb, often with 地.

title: Opening or separating with V + 开
pattern: 动词 + 开
explanation: 开 (kāi) after a verb shows something opens up or moves apart — "push open, move away, separate". It's a common resultative complement, as in 推开 (push open), 走开 (go away), and 分开 (split apart).

title: Always with 总是
pattern: (主语) + 总是 + 动词短语
explanation: 总是 (zǒngshì) means "always" — describing something that happens every time, without exception. It goes right before the verb, similar to 老是 but more neutral in tone.

title: Comprehensively with 全面
pattern: 全面 + 动词
explanation: 全面 (quánmiàn) means "comprehensively, in all respects" — describing an action or understanding that covers every aspect, not just part of it. It goes right before the verb.

title: Bringing out with V + 出
pattern: 动词 + 出
explanation: 出 (chū) after a verb shows something comes out or is revealed through the action — "figure out, point out, take out". It's a very productive resultative complement, seen in words like 找出, 拿出, 提出, and 指出.
